findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on I/O failure (file missing, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or malformed filesystem input aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error the caller can handle
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV data (e.g. "alice,hello") panics the process instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use .map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue) on the parse call and propagate through a Result return type

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) embeds side-effecting I/O inside the data-loading/shard-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure domain logic leaks logging to stdout; the function is not composable, not testable in isolation, and side effects cannot be controlled or suppressed in production
findings.fix: remove println! entirely from the core; if logging is needed, delegate it to the shell layer outside this function

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 performs a lossy cast from u32 to u16; values >65535 silently truncate
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 value like 70000 wraps to 34468, corrupting the domain value with no error signal or overflow detection
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::Overflow) to reject out-of-range values with a typed error

findings.problem: raw String and u16 primitives cross the parse boundary directly; the domain struct accepts unvalidated name strings and unbounded u16 values with no smart constructor or newtype guard
findings.failure_mode: any caller can construct a Record with an empty name, whitespace-only name, or any u16 value bypassing domain invariants; illegal domain states are representable
findings.fix: introduce a Name newtype with a fallible smart constructor that validates non-empty and trims; replace Record fields with Name and a bounded u16 variant

findings.problem: path: &str is a raw primitive that crosses the parse boundary without validation or fallible smart constructor; the function signature exposes no typed error domain
findings.failure_mode: callers can pass empty, null, or hostile path strings directly; the function itself cannot communicate structured failures for bad input, missing files, or parse errors
findings.fix: accept a validated path type or return Result<..., LoadError>; the shell layer should validate the path string before calling into core

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] use unchecked indexing on a split result; a line with fewer than 2 commas panics
findings.failure_mode: a CSV line like "only_onename" or an empty line panics via index-out-of-bounds instead of returning a typed ParseError
findings.fix: use parts.get(0) and parts.get(1).ok_or(ParseError::Invalid) or restructure with split_once(',') to avoid intermediate Vec and indexing entirely

findings.problem: no try_reserve, no domain cap, no bounded allocation; every line allocates a Vec<String> and the outer collect() grows unboundedly from any file size
findings.failure_mode: a large or malicious input file causes unbounded heap allocation and OOM without graceful error handling
findings.fix: validate a domain max_rows cap before the loop, use Vec::new() then out.try_reserve(cap).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? after cap validation, enforce per-row max, and use split_once(',') with no intermediate Vec

findings.problem: load_shards fuses file I/O (fs::read_to_string), parsing (split/collect), logging (println!), and domain construction (Record) into a single function
findings.failure_mode: violates Data/Calculations/Actions separation; pure parsing logic cannot be tested independently of the filesystem, and side effects prevent deterministic reasoning
findings.fix: split into: (1) shell layer handles fs::read_to_string and delegates to core; (2) pure parse_shard_line function takes a &str and returns Result<Record, ParseError>; (3) shell iterates lines and collects results

findings.problem: use std::fs brings the entire filesystem module into scope for I/O inside what should be core logic
findings.failure_mode: core logic depends directly on filesystem I/O, making it untestable in pure contexts and violating the imperative shell / pure core boundary
findings.fix: remove std::fs import from the core module; shell layer handles all fs::read_to_string and passes parsed strings or domain types to pure core functions

findings.failure_mode: without workload baseline or allocation measurements, performance characteristics are unknown and cannot be validated against Holzman allocation discipline requirements
findings.fix: add a benchmark measuring load_shards against realistic shard file sizes; profile allocation hot path; report bytes/sec and peak memory
